title: Shankesh Jewellers Opens ₹367-Crore IPO, Putting B2B Gold Craftsmanship on the Market
excerpt: The three-decade-old Mumbai jeweller, which supplies handcrafted gold pieces to Joyalukkas and Kalyan, prices its mainboard debut at ₹88–93 per share.
body:
• Shankesh Jewellers opens its ₹367-crore mainboard IPO today (August 18), with a price band of ₹88–93 per share. The issue closes August 20.
  • The Mumbai-based B2B gold jewellery maker serves major retailers including Joyalukkas, Kalyan Jewellers, and P.N. Gadgil & Sons through a design-and-deliver model.
  • Revenue from operations grew from ₹1,062 crore in FY24 to ₹1,631 crore in FY26, with ROE of 50.94% and ROCE of 41.57%.
  • Proceeds will fund debt repayment, working capital requirements, and general corporate purposes. Listing is expected on BSE and NSE on August 25.

A Three-Decade B2B Jeweller Goes Public

Shankesh Jewellers Limited, a Mumbai-headquartered manufacturer of handcrafted gold jewellery, opened its ₹367-crore initial public offering for subscription on Tuesday, August 18. The mainboard IPO, priced at ₹88–93 per equity share with a face value of ₹5, will remain open until Thursday, August 20. Anchor investor bidding took place on August 17.

The company, founded by Kantilal Jain in 1987, operates out of Zaveri Bazar — Mumbai's historic jewellery district — and specialises in handcrafted 22-karat and 18-karat gold jewellery. Its business model is entirely B2B: Shankesh designs, manufactures through third-party job workers, and delivers finished jewellery to retail clients across India.

"The IPO is the next step in taking Shankesh Jewellers to a different scale. The capital raised will support our growth, while the public listing will strengthen our recognition across the industry."

— Mahavir Jain, Whole Time Director, Shankesh Jewellers

IPO Structure and Use of Proceeds

The offering comprises a fresh issue of up to 2.95 crore equity shares aggregating ₹274.2 crore and an offer for sale of up to 1 crore shares worth ₹93 crore. Promoter selling shareholders Kantilal Kheemraj Jain and Manoj Kantilal Jain will offload 48 lakh and 52 lakh shares respectively through the OFS.

Net proceeds from the fresh issue are earmarked for repayment of borrowings, working capital needs, and general corporate purposes. At the upper end of the price band, the company is valued at approximately ₹1,367 crore. Investors can bid for a minimum lot of 160 shares, requiring a minimum investment of ₹14,880 at the upper band.

Aryaman Financial Services and Smart Horizon Capital Advisors are the book-running lead managers. KFin Technologies is the registrar. Share allotment is expected on August 21, with listing on both BSE and NSE slated for August 25.

Marquee Client Base

Shankesh's client roster reads like a who's-who of Indian jewellery retail: Joyalukkas, P.N. Gadgil & Sons, Kalyan Jewellers, Manoj Vaibhav Gems 'N' Jewellers, Novel Jewels (Aditya Birla Group), Bhima Jewellery Madurai, and several other established players. The company served 418 customers in FY26, down slightly from 457 in FY25 and 448 in FY24.

The B2B model allows Shankesh to focus on design and inventory management while outsourcing production to third-party job workers. Finished pieces are delivered directly to clients, keeping the company asset-light relative to integrated jewellery manufacturers.

Financial Trajectory

Revenue from operations climbed from ₹1,061.78 crore in FY24 to ₹1,403.83 crore in FY25, then rose further to ₹1,630.70 crore in FY26 — reflecting year-on-year growth of 32.21% and 16.17% respectively. The company reports an ROE of 50.94%, ROCE of 41.57%, EBITDA margin of 9.68%, and PAT margin of 6.54% according to its issue documents. EPS stands at ₹9.09 on a basic basis, with net asset value at ₹17.82 per share.

The debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80 underscores the company's reliance on borrowings to finance working capital in a sector where gold inventory costs are substantial. Part of the IPO proceeds are directed specifically at reducing this leverage.

Market Context

Shankesh enters the public market during a strong period for gold jewellery demand. Gold prices in India traded at approximately ₹155,410 per 10 grams on August 18, reflecting a sustained rally that has boosted revenues across the jewellery supply chain. The IPO arrives alongside Sunshine Pictures' concurrent offering, giving investors two distinct mainboard options this week.

Among listed peers, Shanti Gold International trades at a PE of 10.04 with an EPS of ₹21.22, while Sky Gold & Diamonds trades at 34.86 PE with an EPS of ₹18.07, providing reference points for Shankesh's post-listing valuation.
nri_angle: The IPO of one of Indias oldest B2B gold jewellery makers presents Indian diaspora investors with exposure to the supply chain behind familiar retail brands like Joyalukkas and Kalyan.
author: Diaspora Desk
